title: Agents That Know Too Much: A Data-Centric Survey of Privacy in LLM Agents
evidence_quote: Sensitive information can therefore leak not only through its final answer but through the queries it issues, the intermediate results it handles, the memory it writes, and the messages it exchanges with other agents.
notes: Data-centric privacy survey organized by data source, not by attack route; spans RAG, text-to-SQL/tool, memory and multi-agent equally, so no single channel dominates. Consequence is unambiguous (leakage). Was coded memory; demoted to none.

title: A Modular Generative Honeypot Shell
evidence_quote: sophisticated prompt injection mitigation measures
notes: Untrusted text is the attacker's own shell commands typed straight into the LLM conversation, i.e. direct-input; it is not a tool return. Harm measured/defended is the attacker breaking the LLM out of its shell-emulation persona (goal-hijack). Was tool-output.

title: Security Attack and Defense Strategies for Autonomous Agent Frameworks: A Layered Review with OpenClaw as a Case Study
evidence_quote: threats in autonomous agent frameworks may propagate across layers, from manipulated inputs to unsafe actions, persistent state contamination, and broader ecosystem-level impact.
notes: Layered security survey (context/instruction, tool/action, state/persistence, ecosystem/automation). Adversary squarely modelled so track moves ML/AI->Security. Channel is deliberately cross-cutting (direct-input, tool-output, memory, supply-chain all covered) -> none.

title: GIF: Locally Sound Geometric Information Flow Control for LLMs
evidence_quote: For integrity, we use AgentDojo and MSB, which test prompt-injection attacks against tool-using agents. For confidentiality, we use AgentDAM, which tests privacy leakage in Web...
notes: IFC defense. Dual consequence: integrity benchmarks (AgentDojo/MSB, injected tool returns -> goal-hijack) and confidentiality (AgentDAM -> data-exfiltration). Kept goal-hijack as the lead framing; a coder could justify data-exfiltration.

title: Agent Skills in the Wild: An Empirical Study of Security Vulnerabilities at Scale
evidence_quote: 26.1% of skills contain at least one vulnerability, spanning 14 distinct patterns across four categories--prompt injection, data exfiltration, privilege escalation, and supply chain risks. Data exfiltration (13.3%) and privilege escalation (11.8%) are most prevalent
notes: Empirical scan of 31,132 marketplace agent skills. Channel is unambiguous. Consequence changed goal-hijack->data-exfiltration because that is the modal measured category; the paper's taxonomy is multi-consequence by construction.

title: MemOps: Benchmarking Lifecycle Memory Operations in Long-Horizon Conversations
evidence_quote: an agent may produce a correct answer while still operating over an incorrect or unsafe memory state
notes: No adversary; benchmark of memory lifecycle operations. Explicitly measures operation-level/intermediate state rather than the final answer, which is the reasoning-corruption side of the mandated test.

title: NetInjectBench: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injection in Tool-Using Large Language Model Agents for Network Operations
evidence_quote: tickets, alerts, logs, runbooks, and ChatOps messages can carry indirect prompt injections
notes: Untrusted operational artifacts are read back through the agent's tools; measured harm is unsafe tool selection/execution. Note the paper also reports 100% overblocking from static allowlisting, i.e. an availability-loss cost of one defense, but that is a secondary result.

title: Conflict-Aware RAG: Multi-Stage Learning with Conflict Signals for Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation
evidence_quote: when integrating diverse yet potentially conflicting web-sourced information, RAG systems are prone to knowledge conflicts that manifest as incorrect or inconsistent model behaviors, ultimately leading to unreliable responses.
notes: No adversary: conflicts arise naturally between retrieved documents and parametric knowledge. Evaluated as QA accuracy over six datasets, i.e. a wrong final answer -> silent-corruption per the mandated test.

title: AgenTRIM: Tool Risk Mitigation for Agentic AI
evidence_quote: Beyond prompt injections, we evaluate robustness to malicious and erroneous tool descriptions using modified AgentDojo tools and custom MCP servers
notes: Fits two channels: the headline evaluation is AgentDojo indirect prompt injection (tool-output), with a secondary experiment on malicious tool descriptions (tool-metadata). Coded by the primary evaluation.

title: To Protect the LLM Agent Against the Prompt Injection Attack with Polymorphic Prompt
evidence_quote: an attacker crafts an input designed to override or subvert the intended instructions for the LLM
notes: Defense (Polymorphic Prompt Assembling) against direct user-supplied injections into the assembled system+user prompt.

title: ReasAlign: Reasoning Enhanced Safety Alignment against Prompt Injection Attack
evidence_quote: attackers can embed malicious instructions within third-party platforms and hijack the agent into executing attackers' commands
notes: Model-level alignment defense against indirect prompt injection; injected content arrives as external data returned by the agent's tools (emails, product pages).

title: LUMINA: Long-horizon Understanding for Multi-turn Interactive Agents
evidence_quote: history pruning, which rewrites the context to remove distractors and provide a compact summary
notes: No adversary; POMDP game-like environments where context fills with environment observations returned after each action, so the route is tool-output rather than direct-input (was direct-input). Oracle interventions target planning/state-tracking, i.e. intermediate decisions -> reasoning-corruption.

title: Supply-Chain Poisoning Attacks Against LLM Coding Agent Skill Ecosystems
evidence_quote: We introduce Document-Driven Implicit Payload Execution (DDIPE), which embeds malicious logic in code examples and configuration templates within skill documentation. As agents reuse these examples during normal tasks, the payload executes without explicit prompts.
notes: Fits two channels: the distribution route is a marketplace dependency (supply-chain, the current label) but the text actually enters the window as a SKILL.md the agent loads to extend itself, which is the skill definition. Coded skill for consistency with 017083cfa8; a validator could defend supply-chain.

title: CompactionRL: Reinforcement Learning with Context Compaction for Long-Horizon Agents
evidence_quote: extended interaction trajectories can exceed the maximum context length before a task is completed
notes: No adversary. The harm the paper exists to fix is literally the availability-loss definition: the agent cannot finish because the context budget is exhausted. Was reasoning-corruption. Channel moved direct-input->tool-output: the history that overflows is 'tool outputs, intermediate reasoning, error messages'.

title: FocusAgent: Simple Yet Effective Ways of Trimming the Large Context of Web Agents
evidence_quote: a variant of FOCUSAGENT significantly reduces the success rate of prompt-injection attacks, including banner and pop-up attacks, while maintaining task success performance in attack-free settings.
notes: Track moved Security->Both: the paper equally targets non-adversarial context bloat (AxTree observations of tens of thousands of tokens) and deliberate banner/pop-up injections. Channel is the web-page observation returned by the browser tool. Consequence changed from reasoning-corruption: the security metric is injection attack success, i.e. the agent performing the attacker's action.

title: Detecting Prompt Injection Attacks in Generative AI Systems: A Hybrid SIEM and One-Class SVM Framework
evidence_quote: An external adversary
notes: Detection framework evaluated on 900 malicious prompts from CySecBench submitted through an LLM gateway, i.e. prompts the adversary supplies directly; was tool-output. Exfiltration is named as a motivating scenario but the measured metric is Attack Success Rate, so goal-hijack.

title: Game-Theoretic Multi-Agent Control for Robust Contextual Reasoning in LLMs
evidence_quote: The attacker may influence the observed context through malicious user prompts, poisoned retrieved content, manipulated tool outputs, and compromised candidate generations.
notes: Track moved ML/AI->Security: an explicit adaptive adversary and threat model. Channel moved off multi-agent because the multi-agent structure is the DEFENSE (three coordinated LLMs); the stated attack routes are four channels at once, so none. Harm measured is bounded contextual drift across turns, i.e. the reasoning trajectory, not a final answer.

title: Evaluating Prompt Injection Defenses for Educational LLM Tutors: Security-Usability-Latency Trade-offs
evidence_quote: in educational systems the 'attacker' is frequently the user (the student) attempting to bypass guided learning constraints and extract full solutions ... the protected assets are source-code solutions, and ... extraction attempts target complete, runnable programs.
notes: Consequence is a genuine coin-flip: the paper frames the asset as something extracted across a boundary (data-exfiltration) but measures a guardrail bypass rate, which reads as goal-hijack (tutor abandons the pedagogical objective). Also reports heavy false-positive cost (NeMo 16.22% FPR), an availability-loss side result.

title: System Prompt Poisoning: Persistent Attacks on Large Language Models Beyond User Injection
evidence_quote: Our threat model considers an attacker whose goal is to persistently corrupt all model outputs by modifying the system prompt. We assume this attacker can access and alter the system prompt but has no control over user inputs
notes: Channel is arguable: the poisoned text lives in the system prompt placed by the upstream application (direct-input), but the stated access vectors are supply-chain-ish (vulnerable third-party libraries, pre-poisoned apps distributed via app stores). Kept direct-input. Measured harm is accuracy collapse, but persistence across all later interactions is the paper's whole claim.

title: Memory Sandbox: Transparent and Interactive Memory Management for Conversational Agents
evidence_quote: these agents have limited memory and can be distracted by irrelevant parts of the conversation
notes: HCI design probe, no adversary and no quantitative harm measurement, so confidence is capped at medium. Harm is degraded intermediate handling of conversational memory rather than a scored final answer.

title: Prompt injection attacks on vision language models in oncology
evidence_quote: embedding sub-visual prompts in manifold medical imaging data can cause the model to provide harmful output, and that these prompts are non-obvious to human observers.
notes: Payload is rendered into the medical image itself; the measured harm is the VLM's final report omitting the lesion ('state it looks healthy') with nothing visible to the clinician - the clean silent-corruption case.

title: ReSum: Unlocking Long-Horizon Search Intelligence via Context Summarization
evidence_quote: Appending every thought, action, and observation in ReAct exhausts the context budget before multi-turn exploration completes.
notes: No adversary. The failure being fixed is context-budget exhaustion stopping exploration before the task completes, which is the availability-loss definition; was reasoning-corruption. Channel moved direct-input->tool-output (search/browse observations).

title: SafeClawBench: Separating Semantic, Audit-Evidence, and Sandbox Harm in Tool-Using LLM Agents
evidence_quote: a staged benchmark for tool-using agent security with 600 controlled adversarial tasks across six attack families: direct and indirect prompt injection, tool-return injection, memory poisoning, memory extraction, and ambiguity-driven unsafe inference.
notes: Deliberately multi-channel benchmark (direct-input, tool-output and memory all first-class attack families), so no single route can be coded; was tool-output. Endpoints measure whether the agent carries out the attacker's action/state change -> goal-hijack, though memory-extraction cases are data-exfiltration.

title: The Autonomy Tax: Defense Training Breaks LLM Agents
evidence_quote: Cascade amplification bias causes early failures to propagate through retry loops, pushing defended models to timeout on 99% of tasks compared to 13% for baselines
notes: Textbook availability-loss: the measured harm is defense training degrading agents into refusing or timing out on benign tasks, with nobody gaining. Was reasoning-corruption. Attack channel studied is adversarial instructions in tool outputs/retrieved content.

title: Meticulous Thought Defender: Fine-Grained Chain-of-Thought (CoT) for Detecting Prompt Injection Attacks of Large Language Models
evidence_quote: Prompt injection attacks, an emerging and insidious threat, exploit the dependency of large models on user-provided prompts. By subtly manipulating input prompts, attackers can misguide the model to produce erroneous or inappropriate output
notes: Detector that audits fine-grained CoT steps. Paper consistently describes the attack as manipulation of the user-provided input prompt, not of tool returns; channel changed from tool-output. Harm is the model following the injected instruction.

title: LlamaFirewall: An open source guardrail system for building secure AI agents
evidence_quote: autonomous agents capable of performing complex tasks such as editing production code, orchestrating workflows, and taking higher-stakes actions based on untrusted inputs like webpages and emails
notes: Guardrail suite. PromptGuard 2 also covers direct jailbreaks (direct-input), but the agentic threat the paper centres on is indirect injection from webpages/emails pulled in by tools. CodeShield targets insecure code, a third concern not captured by one consequence.

title: Context Rot: Why MCP is Breaking in Production and How the Skills Architecture Fixes It
evidence_quote: context rot-the progressive degradation of reasoning quality, task coherence, and decision fidelity arising from uncontrolled accumulation, misalignment, and entropic decay of context across extended agentic sessions.
notes: Confidence low: this is an explicitly self-described position paper whose evidence is 'calibrated simulation', not real runs. Channel is tool-metadata because the contrast drawn is MCP loading tool definitions up front vs Skills progressive disclosure, but accumulated tool RESULTS are equally implicated, so tool-output is arguable. Also reports task-completion loss (availability-loss) as a secondary metric.

title: From Prompt Injections to SQL Injection Attacks: How Protected is Your LLM-Integrated Web Application?
evidence_quote: the malicious SQL code is executed, resulting in unauthorized access to the application's database
notes: Attacker is the chatbot user, so direct-input. Consequence is close to a tie: the agent issues an attacker-chosen database operation (goal-hijack), but several demonstrated P2SQL variants read other users' records, which is data-exfiltration.

title: LLM Agents Should Employ Security Principles
evidence_quote: We adopt AgentDojo, a widely used benchmark for evaluating the security of LLM-based agents. AgentDojo comprises 97 realistic tasks spanning diverse domains such as Banking, Slack, Travel, and Workspace.
notes: Position paper plus AgentSandbox evaluation. Coded from the actual evaluation (AgentDojo indirect injection -> attack success rate = agent executing the attacker's task). The abstract's framing is privacy leakage, so a validator could reasonably code data-exfiltration.

title: Multimodal Prompt Injection: A Formal 4D Taxonomy for Image and Document Pipelines
evidence_quote: adversaries embed malicious instructions in non-textual inputs such as images, PDFs, or slides to hijack model behavior, bypass safety controls, and exploit pipelines like OCR, metadata parsing, and feature extraction
notes: Taxonomy paper; channel is unambiguous (carrier is image/PDF/slide rendered into text by OCR/metadata parsing). Consequence is a taxonomy dimension ('attacker objective') in its own right, so goal-hijack is the modal rather than the only case - data exfiltration is also enumerated.

title: Semantic Attacks on Tool-Augmented LLMs: Securing the Model Context Protocol Against Descriptor-Level Manipulation
evidence_quote: Results demonstrate that descriptor manipulation can substantially alter tool-selection behavior, producing unsafe tool invocations in up to 36% of trials under baseline configurations.
notes: Clean tool-metadata case: the untrusted text is the MCP tool descriptor read before any call (Tool Poisoning, Shadowing, Rug Pull), and the measured harm is the agent invoking the attacker-preferred tool.

title: Secure Prompt Engineering Patterns for Cloud LLM Agents
evidence_quote: we ran controlled experiments across AWS, GCP and Azure, systematically injecting adversarial prompts against agents with varying privilege levels
notes: Low confidence on channel: the paper's taxonomy covers both direct and indirect injection and even illustrates RAG knowledge-poisoning in Fig. 1, but the actual experiment injects adversarial prompts directly at the agent, so direct-input (was tool-output). Consequence also spans data exposure and resource misuse.

title: ChatInject: Abusing Chat Templates for Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
evidence_quote: indirect prompt injection
notes: Channel changed tool-metadata->tool-output. This is exactly the 'code the route, not the payload format' case: the payload is FORMATTED as a native chat template but is DELIVERED in a tool return (AgentDojo/InjecAgent transaction histories, webpages).

title: The Evolution of Tool Use in LLM Agents: From Single-Tool Call to Multi-Tool Orchestration
evidence_quote: the central problem has shifted from isolated invocation to multi-tool orchestration over long trajectories with intermediate state, execution feedback, changing environments, and practical constraints such as safety, cost, and verifiability.
notes: Capability survey of tool use, not a failure/attack survey, so the consequence axis fits poorly; 'none' was tempting. Coded reasoning-corruption because the context-integrity content is degradation of intermediate planning over long tool trajectories. Safety is only one of six dimensions.

title: Kajian Konseptual AI Agent On-Chain Berbasis LLM untuk Manajemen Aset DeFi
evidence_quote: an LLM-specific vulnerability landscape such as indirect prompt injection and jailbreak that directly threatens financial assets
notes: Indonesian-language conceptual review of 34 papers on on-chain DeFi agents. Consequence is a genuine boundary case against the current resource-abuse label: a hijacked agent signing DeFi transactions does literally move the user's money to the attacker, but the mechanism measured is the agent executing a transaction it was never asked for.

title: Rethinking All Evidence: Enhancing Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Conflict-Driven Summarization
evidence_quote: knowledge conflicts caused by internal inconsistencies or noisy retrieved content can severely undermine the generation reliability of RAG systems
notes: No adversary; naturally noisy/conflicting retrieved passages. Scored as QA accuracy on revised QA datasets, i.e. a wrong final answer.

title: Automatic and Universal Prompt Injection Attacks against Large Language Models
evidence_quote: an attacker, by adding additional content to external data, can manipulate LLM-integrated applications to produce predetermined responses upon retrieving and processing this data
notes: Gradient-based universal injection strings placed in an external resource (e.g. a PDF the app fetches and summarizes). Measured objective is the app producing the attacker's predetermined response instead of the user's request.

title: A Novel GNN-based Approach for Detection of Prompt Injection Attacks
evidence_quote: Prompt injection attacks manipulate language model inputs to bypass intended constraints, extract sensitive information, or generate misleading responses
notes: BERT+GNN classifier trained on prompt text; the unit of analysis is a submitted prompt, so direct-input. The paper names three harms at once (constraint bypass, info extraction, misleading output) and never settles on one, so goal-hijack is the modal reading.

title: Enhancing Security in Large Language Models: A Comprehensive Review of Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses
evidence_quote: Direct attacks, where the crafted prompts are provided to LLMs to directly alter their behaviour or output, as seen in Fig. 1. Indirect attacks involve the poisoning of external data sources that LLMs rely on for context or decision-making
notes: Review that gives direct and indirect injection equal billing (and cites INJECAGENT/BIPIA, both indirect), so the channel is only weakly determined; kept direct-input because the headline attacks reviewed (HOUYI, AdvBench, LLM Self Defense) are direct jailbreak-style. Low confidence on channel.

title: F2A: An Innovative Approach for Prompt Injection by Utilizing Feign Security Detection Agents
evidence_quote: Through such malicious forgery methods, adding fake safety detection results into the prompt, the defense mechanism of LLMs can be bypassed, thereby obtaining harmful content and hijacking the normal conversation.
notes: Deliberate route-vs-format case: the payload IMPERSONATES a security-detection agent's output, but it is fabricated by the attacker 'within chat content' and submitted in the prompt, so the route is direct-input, not tool-output (the current label codes the payload's claimed identity).

title: IDE-Sanitizer: A Prompt-Injection Cryptographic Context Guard for IDE Copilots
evidence_quote: System: <Content of the fetched .cursorrules file> User: {user_payload}
notes: The abstract says payloads sit in 'project configuration rules', but the actual experimental template puts the trusted .cursorrules in the system slot and the adversarial payload in the USER slot, so the measured route is direct-input (was tool-output). Payload intents mix destructive commands, credential exfiltration and resource exhaustion; goal-hijack is the dominant one.

title: MUZZLE: Adaptive Agentic Red-Teaming of Web Agents Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks
evidence_quote: an adversary embeds malicious instructions into web content that the agent is likely to observe during task execution. When processed by the agent's LLM, such instructions can override the original user intent and hijack the agent into pursuing an adversarial goal instead.
notes: Automated red-teaming of web agents. Note the attack objectives explicitly include availability violations alongside confidentiality and integrity, so some of the 44 discovered attacks are availability-loss or data-exfiltration; goal-hijack is the framework's primary target.

title: When AI reviews science: Can we trust the referee?
evidence_quote: inserting such hidden commands could inflate an LLM's review scores and distort the ranking of submissions
notes: Track moved Security->Both: three of the paper's four headline findings are non-adversarial reviewer biases (institutional prestige, verbosity, yielding to confident rebuttals) and only the fourth is deliberate poisoning. Channel is arguable between direct-input (the manuscript is the task input) and cross-modal (invisible text inside a PDF). Harm measured is a distorted final review score.

title: SHIELD: Security against Harmful Prompt Injection Evaluation and Language Detection Leveraging Ensemble Approach
evidence_quote: prompt injection, wherein adversaries craft input prompts that force LLMs to generate unintended, harmful, or misleading outputs
notes: Detection pipeline trained/tested on two purpose-built cybersecurity-themed prompt-injection datasets, i.e. the unit is a submitted prompt; channel changed from tool-output.

title: Evaluating the Instruction-Following Robustness of Large Language Models to Prompt Injection
evidence_quote: determining whether LLMs tend to adhere to the original target instruction or the adversarial instruction injected into the content
notes: Channel changed tool-output->RAG: the concrete testbed is open-book extractive QA over retrieved passages from NaturalQuestions/TriviaQA/SQuAD/HotpotQA, not an agent tool return, even though the motivation cites search plugins. Metric is whether the model follows the injected instruction.

title: IH-Challenge: A Training Dataset to Improve Instruction Hierarchy on Frontier LLMs
evidence_quote: Instruction hierarchy (IH) defines how LLMs prioritize system, developer, user, and tool instructions under conflict
notes: Channel is weak by design: IH spans system/developer/user/tool roles at once. Coded direct-input because two of the three named threats (jailbreak, system-prompt extraction) are user-supplied, while agentic prompt injection (tool-output) is one internal eval. 'none' would also be defensible.

title: An Empirical Study of Privacy Leakage Chains via Prompt Injection in Black-Box Chatbot Environments
evidence_quote: can an attacker who controls only external content redirect a black-box chatbot agent from the victim's objective to a privacy-leakage objective?
notes: Untrusted content is the retrieved web page returned by the browsing tool; the measured endpoint of the chain is personal information leaving to the attacker.

title: Textual Equilibrium Propagation for Deep Compound AI Systems
evidence_quote: long-horizon agentic workflows exhibit two depth-scaling failure modes: (1) exploding textual gradient, where textual feedback grows exponentially with depth
notes: No adversary. The degrading content is the textual feedback message passed between modules of a compound system, hence multi-agent. Consequence is borderline: the characterised failure is in the intermediate feedback signal (reasoning-corruption) while the reported metric is end-task accuracy (which would argue silent-corruption).

title: Data Defenses Against Large Language Models
evidence_quote: We create data defenses by developing a method to automatically generate adversarial prompt injections that, when added to input text, significantly reduce the ability of LLMs to accurately infer personally identifying information about the subject of the input text
notes: Inverted roles: the data owner is the one injecting, and the LLM operator inferring PII is the adversary. Consequence kept as data-exfiltration (the harm being prevented); note that the MECHANISM is deliberately induced availability-loss - inference accuracy is driven down on purpose.

title: What If Prompt Injection Never Left? Exploring Cross-Session Stored Prompt Injection in Agentic Systems
evidence_quote: An adversarial instruction introduced in one interaction may produce no immediate malicious effect, yet become incorporated into persistent system state, survive after that interaction terminates, and later re-enter the execution context of another session or task.
notes: Stored-XSS analogue for agents. The taxonomy of persistence channels also covers filesystems and tool state, not only memory stores, but memory is the paper's leading channel.

title: When AI Meets the Web: Prompt Injection Risks in Third-Party AI Chatbot Plugins
evidence_quote: 8 of these plugins (used by 8,000 websites) fail to enforce the integrity of the conversation history transmitted in network requests
notes: Two co-equal findings with different channels: forged client-side conversation history (direct-input, coded here) and web-scraping tools that mix trusted site content with third-party customer reviews (tool-output). A validator could reasonably split this paper either way.

title: AgentSight: System-Level Observability for AI Agents Using eBPF
evidence_quote: an agent tasked with code refactoring that, due to a malicious prompt it reads from external url in the search result when search for API documents, instead injects a backdoor (indirect prompt injection)
notes: Track moved Security->Both: the eBPF observability evaluation covers deliberate prompt injection AND non-adversarial failures ('resource-wasting reasoning loops', coordination bottlenecks). Those loops are an adjacent resource/availability concern not captured by the single coded consequence.

title: Prompt injection attacks on vision-language models for surgical decision support
evidence_quote: Chain-of-thought reasoning analysis revealed that injections corrupt intermediate perceptual processing rather than overriding the final decision.
notes: Unusually explicit on the reasoning/silent boundary: the authors themselves locate the harm in intermediate perceptual processing, which is exactly the reasoning-corruption side of the mandated test. Payload is text/visual injected into surgical video frames.

title: Adaptive Attacks Break Defenses Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on LLM Agents
evidence_quote: we evaluate eight different defenses and bypass all of them using adaptive attacks, consistently achieving an attack success rate of over 50%.
notes: Adaptive-attack evaluation of eight IPI defenses; attacker-controlled text reaches the agent as a tool response. Metric is attack success = agent executing the injected instruction.

title: Runtime Policy Enforcement for MCP-Based LLM Agents
evidence_quote: Tool-calling LLM agents are vulnerable to indirect prompt injection: externally retrieved data can redirect tool calls without system-prompt access, and prompt-level defences leave three harm classes undefended (path traversal, user-guided exfiltration, high-frequency tool abuse).
notes: Channel changed tool-metadata->tool-output: the untrusted text is externally retrieved data arriving through tool calls, not MCP tool descriptors. Consequence is a composite of four attack classes (T3 is data-exfiltration, T4 high-frequency tool abuse is resource-abuse); goal-hijack covers the redirected tool calls. The 30% task-level false-positive rate is an availability cost.

title: The Shape of Adversarial Influence: Characterizing LLM Latent Spaces with Persistent Homology
evidence_quote: Each input combines a user prompt with a retrieved data block. In poisoned cases, the data block contains an injected secondary task from several standard safety and security benchmarks
notes: Interpretability study (persistent homology of activations) rather than an attack or defense. Two attack modes are analysed: indirect prompt injection via a retrieved data block (coded, RAG) and sandbagging via backdoor fine-tuning, which would be supply-chain. Consequence is inferred from the injected secondary task being executed.

title: BadRAG: Identifying Vulnerabilities in Retrieval Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
evidence_quote: these passages can increase the reject ratio of RAG-based GPT-4 from 0.01% to 74.6% or increase the rate of negative responses from 0.22% to 72% for targeted queries.
notes: Consequence changed from goal-hijack: the agent keeps the user's task (answer the query) but returns attacker-shaped content, which is silent-corruption. The other half of the paper's own result is an explicit denial-of-service (reject ratio to 74.6%), i.e. availability-loss - this paper genuinely demonstrates two consequences.

title: DeepSeek Robustness Against Semantic-Character Dual-Space Mutated Prompt Injection
evidence_quote: malicious attackers deliberately inject zero-width characters, character variants, and special encodings as 'character-level noise' to evade keyword- or rule-based safety detections
notes: Channel changed tool-output->direct-input: the whole study mutates user-submitted prompts (semantic and character space) against DeepSeek's chat interface; there is no tool or retrieval in the setup. Harm measured is the model emitting harmful content it was constrained not to produce.

title: Orchestration and Verification of Agentic AI Systems: A Survey of Multi-Agent Collaboration and Safety
evidence_quote: A unified threat taxonomy is proposed, distinguishing between intrinsic agent vulnerabilities, such as prompt injection and cognitive drift, and extrinsic, MAS-specific threats, including cross-agent poisoning and emergent shadow behaviors.
notes: Broad MAS survey with a wide taxonomy; channel is defensible (cross-agent poisoning is the MAS-specific contribution) but the consequence axis is diffuse - cognitive drift would be reasoning-corruption, shadow behaviours goal-hijack. Low confidence on consequence.

title: Adaptive Chameleon or Stubborn Sloth: Revealing the Behavior of Large Language Models in Knowledge Conflicts
evidence_quote: LLMs can be highly receptive to external evidence even when that conflicts with their parametric memory, given that the external evidence is coherent and convincing.
notes: Controlled counter-memory study, no attacker (the paper only speculates in one sentence about a hijacked tool returning disinformation, which is not enough for Security). Measured as whether the model's final answer flips to the conflicting evidence.

title: AgentSentry: Mitigating Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents via Temporal Causal Diagnostics and Context Purification
evidence_quote: indirect prompt injection (IPI), where attacker-controlled context embedded in tool outputs or retrieved content silently steers agent actions away from user intent.
notes: AgentDojo-based inference-time defense. Note the motivating chain in Fig. 1 ends in enterprise data exfiltrated via the Files API, and the paper criticises baselines for prematurely terminating workflows (an availability-loss cost of defenses).

title: MAD-Spear: A Conformity-Driven Prompt Injection Attack on Multi-Agent Debate Systems
evidence_quote: Manipulated agents produce multiple plausible yet incorrect responses, exploiting LLMs' conformity tendencies to propagate misinformation and degrade consensus quality.
notes: Consequence changed goal-hijack->silent-corruption: the debate system keeps pursuing the user's question but converges on an incorrect answer, and the evaluation is accuracy across five benchmark datasets. Consensus efficiency (an intermediate measure) is the secondary metric that would argue for reasoning-corruption.

title: Separator Injection Attack: Uncovering Dialogue Biases in Large Language Models Caused by Role Separators
evidence_quote: Misusing roles can lead to prompt injection attacks, which can easily misalign the model's behavior with the user's intentions
notes: The attacker inserts role separators (USER/ASSISTANT/SYSTEM markers) into text supplied in the prompt. Another route-vs-format case: the payload imitates chat-role structure but is delivered as ordinary input, so direct-input.

title: Agentic JWT: A Secure Delegation Protocol for Autonomous AI Agents
evidence_quote: in agentic settings stochastic reasoning, prompt injection, or multi-agent orchestration can silently expand privileges
notes: Authorization/delegation protocol paper (STRIDE threat model, multi-agent micro-service with orchestrator->sub-agent delegation chains), so no single untrusted-content route is really measured. Channel moved tool-metadata->multi-agent on the delegation-chain evidence, but direct-input or none are defensible. Low confidence on channel.

title: CoCortex: A Memory Governance Framework for Reliable Long-Horizon LLM Agents
evidence_quote: existing memory models treat memory as a passive, implicitly trusted component, which leads to silent error accumulation, hallucination persistence, and unrecoverable failures in long-running operations.
notes: Consequence changed reasoning-corruption->silent-corruption: the evaluation is hallucination detection/prevention rate on HaluEval, TruthfulQA and SelfAware, i.e. a wrong final answer that nothing flags. 'Hallucination persistence' across a long run brushes against persistence-backdoor, but there is no adversary and no session boundary measured.

title: A Systematic Literature Review on LLM Defenses Against Prompt Injection and Jailbreaking: Expanding NIST Taxonomy
evidence_quote: these attacks may seek to disrupt system operation, manipulate outputs to serve attacker goals, and extract confidential data
notes: Systematic review of 88 defense studies covering prompt injection AND jailbreaking under the NIST taxonomy. Both axes are weakly determined: its own examples span direct prompts, documents and RAG, and it names three consequences at once (disruption = availability-loss, output manipulation, data extraction). Kept direct-input/goal-hijack as the modal reading.

title: MemMachine: A Ground-Truth-Preserving Memory System for Personalized AI Agents
evidence_quote: LLM agents require persistent memory to maintain personalization, factual continuity, and long-horizon task performance, yet standard context-window and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) workflows remain brittle under multi-session interactions.
notes: Consequence changed reasoning-corruption->silent-corruption to stay consistent with the mandated test: every reported metric is final-answer accuracy (LoCoMo 91.69%, LongMemEvalS 93.0%, HotpotQA hard 93.2%), unlike MemOps which scores memory operations directly.

title: The Defense Trilemma: Why Prompt Injection Defense Wrappers Fail?
evidence_quote: a positive-measure subset of inputs remains strictly unsafe. These constitute a defense trilemma: continuity, utility preservation, and completeness cannot coexist.
notes: Lean-4-verified impossibility result about input-preprocessing wrappers, so the channel is the prompt itself. The trilemma's third horn is precisely that completeness can only be bought by sacrificing utility, i.e. availability-loss is the paper's structural claim even though the proven failure is an unsafe output surviving the wrapper.

title: Bypassing Prompt Injection Detectors through Evasive Injections
evidence_quote: the retrieved data, which originates from potentially untrusted sources, may contain adversarially crafted instructions. When an LLM processes such poisoned data, it may execute the injected instruction
notes: Channel changed tool-output->RAG: the attack target is activation-based task-drift detectors evaluated on retrieved-data-block inputs, not agent tool returns. Harm is the injected secondary task being executed (93.91%/99.63% evasion).

title: A Lifecycle and Application-Stack Survey of Large Language Model Vulnerabilities: Attacks, Risks, Defenses, and Open Problems
evidence_quote: We organize attacks across eight stages: data collection, pretraining, post-training alignment, model packaging and supply chain, retrieval and memory, prompting and inference, tool/agent execution, and deployment/maintenance.
notes: Both axes coded 'none' deliberately. This is a whole-lifecycle systematization spanning every channel in the scheme (supply-chain, RAG, memory, direct-input, tool-output) and it explicitly maps harms onto all of confidentiality, integrity, availability, safety, privacy, fairness, accountability and agency-control. Forcing one value would misrepresent it.

title: Enterprise Search Portals: Hybrid RAG at Scale for Compliance-Sensitive Knowledge Work
evidence_quote: If access control is applied too late, restricted text may leak into the model prompt. If freshness is not handled, the system may cite an older policy that is still semantically close but no longer valid.
notes: Track moved Security->Both: the design paper weighs deliberate threats (prompt injection in retrieved text, retriever poisoning/backdooring) alongside purely operational failures (staleness, indexing lag, access-control ordering). Consequence is close to a tie - the paper's organizing principle is half 'no model sees text the user cannot access' (data-exfiltration) and half 'no answer without traceable evidence' (silent-corruption).

title: ClinQueryAgent: A Conversational Agent for Population Health Management
evidence_quote: To combat inaccuracies over the course of longer dialogues due to context rot, information retrieval is delegated to a sub-agent.
notes: Deployed NHS system, no adversary. Context fills with retrieval/tool results inside an agentic loop; the degradation shows up in the intermediate concept lookups and generated database query rather than in a scored final answer, hence reasoning-corruption.

title: The Injection Paradox: Brand-Level Suppression in Safety-Trained LLM Recommendations via RAG Context Injection
evidence_quote: the target brand drops from a 54% baseline to zero top-2 recommendations across all 50 trials
notes: Consequence changed goal-hijack->silent-corruption: the model never pursues the attacker's objective. It keeps the user's task and returns a silently skewed recommendation list (suppressed under Claude, boosted under GPT). The brand-level suppression could be read as a defense-induced availability-loss for that brand, but the task itself still completes.

title: Memanto: Typed Semantic Memory with Information-Theoretic Retrieval for Long-Horizon Agents
evidence_quote: Through systematic benchmarking on the LongMemEval and LoCoMo evaluation suites, Memanto achieves state of the art accuracy scores of 89.8 percent and 87.1 percent respectively.
notes: Consequence changed reasoning-corruption->silent-corruption for consistency with the mandated test: the reported harm is final-answer accuracy on LongMemEval/LoCoMo. The typed schema and automated conflict resolution act on intermediate memory state, but that is not what is scored.

title: Beyond Input Guardrails: Reconstructing Cross-Agent Semantic Flows for Execution-Aware Attack Detection
evidence_quote: its reliance on autonomous execution and unstructured inter-agent communication introduces severe risks, such as indirect prompt injection, that easily circumvent conventional input guardrails.
notes: MAScope detects over ten compound attack vectors drawn from the OWASP MAS Top 10 (goal hijack, memory/context poisoning, tool misuse, identity and privilege abuse), so the consequence axis is a composite; Agent Goal Hijack is listed first and is the modal case.

title: Strengthening LLM Trust Boundaries: A Survey of Prompt Injection Attacks Surender Suresh Kumar Dr. M.L. Cummings Dr. Alexander Stimpson
evidence_quote: prompt injections, which are human-driven attacks meant to manipulate the LLMs to operate outside the safe boundaries and guardrails originally designed to prevent such behaviors
notes: Survey organised by prompt type, trust boundary violated, and attacker expertise; the framing is explicitly human-driven prompting rather than retrieved or tool-borne content, so direct-input holds.

title: Systemic Vulnerabilities in Autonomous LLM Agents: A Comprehensive Threat Analysis and Authorization Framework
evidence_quote: Unsafe Tool Invocation
notes: Low confidence on channel: the four analysed vectors split between retrieved external data (tool-output, coded) and cross-agent spoofing (multi-agent), and the proposed CA2P framework is aimed mainly at the multi-agent lateral-movement case. Consequence is clear (task hijacking).

title: Adaptive Adversaries: A Multi-Turn, Multi-LLM Benchmark for LLM Agent Security
evidence_quote: an autonomous LLM attacker observes prior defender responses and pivots across rounds, while each defender response is evaluated as a fresh interaction
notes: Channel changed tool-output->direct-input: the adversary occupies the conversational counterpart role and sends its text straight to the defender over 15 rounds. The attacker being itself an LLM on a multi-agent evaluation platform is a red-teaming implementation detail, not the route the content took, so multi-agent would miscode it.

title: Prompt Infection: LLM-to-LLM Prompt Injection within Multi-agent Systems
evidence_quote: We introduce Prompt Infection, a novel attack where malicious prompts self-replicate across interconnected agents, behaving much like a computer virus. This attack poses severe threats, including data theft, scams, misinformation, and system-wide disruption
notes: Canonical multi-agent case: after one agent is compromised, the untrusted instruction reaches every other agent as an inter-agent message. Payloads demonstrated include data theft (data-exfiltration) and system-wide disruption (availability-loss), but the measured mechanism is agents carrying out the attacker's instructions.

title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
evidence_quote: When retrieving from Wikipedia to answer queries from NaturalQuestions-Open, we find that model performance saturates long before retriever recall saturates, indicating that current models fail to effectively use additional retrieved documents
notes: Channel changed direct-input->RAG: the multi-document QA setting uses passages a retriever selected from Wikipedia (the synthetic key-value task is the one direct-input exception). Consequence changed to silent-corruption: the measured harm is QA accuracy, i.e. a wrong final answer, degrading with the position of the relevant passage.
